I've added the flag and gated `checkout()`. I couldn't run a smoke test because Flask isn't installed in this environment, so the change hasn't been run yet.

- **`flags.toml`:** added `new-checkout = false`. It's a kebab-case name declared in `flags.toml`, which is how the project says flags must be set up.
- **`src/api/checkout.py`:** `checkout()` now calls `flags.is_on("new-checkout")` before it does anything else. While the flag is off, `POST /checkout` returns a 404 using the existing `problem()` helper, in the project's `problem+json` error format. When the flag is on, it runs as it did before.

There's no older checkout to fall back to, so I made the endpoint look like it doesn't exist while the flag is off. If you'd rather return a different status, like 403 or 503, or fall back to some other code path, that's a one-line change. To turn the new checkout on, set `new-checkout = true` in `flags.toml`.

Nothing is committed.
